edit_story.story_line: As Steve, I want benchmark tasks scored by whether their generated specs pass, so that I can see whether a model produced the requested behavior rather than merely resolvable code, and decide about Avowry on honest numbers.
As Ari, I want the vocabulary to grow from recurring patterns mined from real codebases and LLM task logs, so that the keywords I find remove work I would otherwise write by hand, in fewer tokens.

As Steve, I want benchmark tasks that measure the work each keyword removes and whether a cold model finds the right keyword, so that I can judge catalogue coverage by useful task outcomes instead of keyword count.

As Steve, I want benchmark tasks that require parallel collection, bounded concurrency, publication and timeout or cancellation, so that I can see whether there is recurring demand and whether named keywords reduce agent work before I direct the language to grow them.

As Steve, I want development benchmark tasks that ask for a stored-record outcome and a published-event outcome, run under today's grammar, so that I can see whether cold models write specs that state the stored record or the event, or hide behind succeeds, before I approve changing the grammar.

As Morgan, I want a generated spec that supplies an in-memory store and an event capture and asserts the stored record and the published event, with the same trace every run, so that I can verify what a program stores and emits from the spec alone, without real infrastructure or flaky results.

As Steve, I want the candidate cheaper models run cold in both arms on the development tasks and the holdouts at the pre-registered N, so that I can see the cheapest model that clears the pass bar per arm and decide whether Phrase saves money through cheaper models.

As Steve, I want the pre-registered modify and fix tasks run cold in both arms at each codebase size, so that I can compare cost and pass rate as the codebase grows and decide whether Phrase's edge widens at scale.

As Steve, I want the two arms grown feature by feature from the same checkpoints by cold models, so that I can compare tokens, attempts and pass rate at each codebase size and decide whether Phrase pays off as a codebase grows.
As Steve, I want Copilot's 30 unavailable holdout rows run once its quota is back, under exactly the original rules, so that the holdout verdict I use to judge Avowry has all three models.
